# BLO-46113 — lexed outward-command match; cover gh api writes, gh pr merge, GitHub MCP

Tracking: [BLO-46113](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-46113)

**Files:** `src/server/env-guard.ts`, `src/server/env-guard.test.ts`

Follow-up to BLO-29965. The lock re-assertion prefilter (`OUTWARD_RE`) matched
raw command text, so a quoted mention of `git push` (an echo, a commit message)
triggered the lock lookup, while `gh api` writes to `pulls` / `git/refs` /
`merges`, `gh pr merge`, and the GitHub MCP write tools bypassed it.

`isOutward()` now runs on the guard's existing `lexShell` words and re-parses a
quoted word only after a command-position wrapper (`sh -c`, `ssh`, `eval`, ...).
Heredocs fed to a shell are still checked through `nested`. The GitHub MCP write
tools get the same lock check; `GUARD_HOOK_MATCHER` routes them to the hook, and
the settings merge re-registers a guard hook whose matcher is stale even when the
guard hash is unchanged. Same fail-open rule as before.

Known ceiling: `gh api graphql` mutations are not matched.
